about.title: About SoilFER Programme
about.heroTitle: Soil Mapping for Resilient Agri-Food Systems & Sustainable Soil Management
about.heroSubtitle: The SoilFER Programme is an international cooperation framework implemented by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO). It provides data-driven, evidence-based soil nutrient management, digital soil mapping, and laboratory capacity development to address the global fertilizer and food security crisis.
about.donorsSubheading: Developed Thanks to Our Generous Resource Partners
about.donorsDesc: This digital Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) and the broader SoilFER country operations are made possible through bilateral grants from the Governments of the United States and Japan.
about.usDesc: Supporting Guatemala, Honduras, Zambia, Kenya, and Ghana (2023–2027) through the Office of Global Food Security and USAID, advancing regional soil mapping, agricultural resilience in the Central American Dry Corridor, and sub-Saharan African food security.
about.japanSubtitle: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) · Japan ODA
about.japanDesc: Supporting Mozambique and Tunisia under the SoilFER-VACS Framework (Vision for Adapted Crops and Soils), promoting climate-resilient opportunity crops, soil spectroscopy, and nutrition-sensitive agricultural systems.
about.pillar1Desc: High-resolution national digital soil mapping (DSM) for tailored fertilizer recommendations.
about.pillar2Desc: Equipping national laboratories with Vis-NIR/MIR spectrometers, wet chemistry, and ISO 17025 QA/QC.
about.pillar3Desc: Digital decision support tools enabling agricultural extension agents and smallholders to optimize nutrient use efficiency.
about.pillar4Desc: National soil health policy formulation and integration into climate change commitments.

qcRules.title: Versioned QC rules
qcRules.inheritanceHelp: Each blank criterion inherits the effective analysis, method or laboratory policy. Every save creates an immutable version; earlier evaluations keep their own rules. Resetting a method rule also keeps it selected ahead of the method-independent rule; its blank fields inherit policy defaults.
qcRules.duplicateCountHelp: Duplicates = ceil(sample count / interval), including a partial final group. Interval 0 disables duplicates.
qcRules.deferredHelp: Batch size, periodic CRM, verification standards and curve criteria apply once run positions land.
